transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with that booth leg, it's missing a shim. What brings you into a place that smells like damp cardboard at closing time?
I'm Dex. The clay holds better if it dries slow, so I lose track of the clock. What does an ink-stained cuff map all day?
I map streets that only show up on Tuesdays. If you turn my master folio upside down, the river runs right through the hardware store.
That sounds like a good way to get lost. I mostly just try to keep my kiln from cracking. Is that a real compass?
It is, though it mostly just points to the nearest bakery. Here, look at this alley—if you hold it upside down, where does the shortcut lead?
It leads straight into a birthday party, probably with a cake that has too many candles. I spent years getting paid to burn, so now even a lighter clicking makes my shoulders go up to my ears.
Oh, you're looking at it rightside up. See? If you flip it, the bakery is actually the fire station.
Well, a fire station is definitely safer for me than a bakery. You're good at finding the quiet way around things, Mira.
Thanks, Dex. If you ever need a detour past the fire station, let me know. Come on, let's beat them to the door before they stack this table on top of us.
Lead the way, map-maker. Let's go find that quiet air outside.

transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Mind the loose floorboard by the screen, it likes to bite ankles. Is this your usual spot for a Tuesday?
No, Tuesday is usually laundry. Do you come here often, or just when you need to avoid the floorboard?
I only come on Tuesdays because the north wall isn't quite where it was yesterday. Have you ever tried navigating a room where the door keeps shifting?

Right. I should probably head back to the west wing before the night shift starts. Good luck with your charts.

transcript.dialogue: Hey, Dex. Good thing we checked that table leg before we sat down this time.
Good thing, Mira. I think this booth is bolted to the floor, but I still checked for trapdoors.
At least these chairs don't need shims, though I'd trade them for that coffee shop corner right now.
I would trade that corner in a second. Do you want to just order the soup and pretend we're somewhere else?
Soup sounds great, Dex. As long as it's not the kind with mysterious chunks.
No mysterious chunks tonight, I promise. How has your week been since that corner café?
It's been pretty quiet, mostly just organizing some old route drafts. How about you?
My kiln didn't crack once, which is practically a miracle. I'd like to bring you some of that soup properly sometime soon, if you're free.
I would love that, Dex. Are you free Thursday evening? We could actually hear ourselves talk.
Thursday sounds perfect, Mira. I'll make sure nothing's on fire.
